Cardinal number 2.

examples.es: Tengo dos hermanos.
examples.en: I have two brothers.

notes: Cardinal number 3.

examples.es: Son las tres de la tarde.
examples.en: It's three in the afternoon.

notes: Cardinal number 4.

examples.es: El gato tiene cuatro patas.
examples.en: The cat has four legs.

notes: Cardinal number 5.

examples.es: Dame cinco minutos.
examples.en: Give me five minutes.

notes: Cardinal number 6.

examples.es: El partido empieza a las seis.
examples.en: The game starts at six.

notes: Cardinal number 7.

examples.es: Hay siete días en la semana.
examples.en: There are seven days in the week.

notes: Cardinal number 8.

examples.es: La tienda cierra a las ocho.
examples.en: The store closes at eight.

notes: Cardinal number 10.

examples.es: Espera diez minutos.
examples.en: Wait ten minutes.

notes: Cardinal number 1000. Also used loosely to mean 'thousands' (a lot).

examples.es: Hay mil razones para sonreír.
examples.en: There are a thousand reasons to smile.

notes: Standard greeting used at any time of day.

examples.es: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo estás?
examples.en: Hello! How are you?

notes: Farewell interjection; also used sarcastically to indicate something is lost or over.

examples.es: Adiós, hasta mañana.
examples.en: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.

notes: Expression of thanks. Feminine plural noun used as a fixed interjection.

examples.es: Muchas gracias por tu ayuda.
examples.en: Thank you very much for your help.

notes: Used to apologise or to get someone's attention politely. Also a noun meaning pardon/forgiveness.

examples.es: Perdón, ¿me puede ayudar?
examples.en: Excuse me, can you help me?

notes: Imperative of oír (to hear); used to get attention. Equivalent to 'hey' or 'listen'.

examples.es: Oye, ¿tienes un momento?
examples.en: Hey, do you have a moment?

notes: Very common Spanish (especially Spain) affirmative. Less common in Latin America where 'okey' or 'está bien' are preferred.

examples.es: Vale, nos vemos a las ocho.
examples.en: Okay, see you at eight.

notes: Agrees in gender and number: todo/toda/todos/todas. As a pronoun means 'everything' or 'everyone'.

examples.es: Todo el mundo sabe eso.
examples.en: Everyone knows that.

notes: Agrees in gender and number: mucho/mucha/muchos/muchas. As an adverb invariable.

examples.es: Hay mucho que aprender.
examples.en: There is a lot to learn.

notes: Agrees in gender and number: poco/poca/pocos/pocas. As an adverb ('a little') invariable.

examples.es: Tengo poco tiempo.
examples.en: I have little time.

notes: Agrees in gender and number: mismo/misma/mismos/mismas. Also used as an intensifier (yo mismo = I myself).

examples.es: Es el mismo problema de siempre.
examples.en: It's the same old problem.

notes: Invariable adjective (no gender/number inflection). Always precedes the noun.

examples.es: Cada día es una nueva oportunidad.
examples.en: Each day is a new opportunity.

notes: Agrees in gender and number: tanto/tanta/tantos/tantas. As an adverb invariable.

examples.es: No esperaba tanto ruido.
examples.en: I didn't expect so much noise.

notes: Relative pronoun referring to people. Plural: quienes. No accent in relative clauses; accent (quién) in questions.

examples.es: La persona quien llamó no dejó mensaje.
examples.en: The person who called didn't leave a message.

notes: Apocopated form of cualquiera used before nouns. Invariable for gender; plural cualquiera(s). Means 'any' in the sense of 'whichever'.

examples.es: Cualquier pregunta es bienvenida.
examples.en: Any question is welcome.

notes: Also spelled quizás (equally correct). Expresses possibility; followed by indicative (more certainty) or subjunctive (less certainty).

examples.es: Quizá tenga razón.
examples.en: Perhaps you are right.

notes: Invariable adverb expressing approximation or near-completion.

examples.es: Casi llegamos a tiempo.
examples.en: We almost made it on time.

notes: Derived from real; used to intensify or confirm.

examples.es: Realmente no lo entiendo.
examples.en: I really don't understand it.

notes: As adjective agrees in number (bastante/bastantes) but not gender. As adverb invariable.

examples.es: Eso es bastante difícil.
examples.en: That is quite difficult.

notes: Followed by indicative or subjunctive depending on degree of certainty.

examples.es: Probablemente llegue tarde.
examples.en: I'll probably arrive late.

notes: Used to affirm precision or to agree emphatically with what someone said.

examples.es: Eso es exactamente lo que quiero.
examples.en: That is exactly what I want.

notes: Derived from simple; often used to downplay or clarify.

examples.es: Simplemente di la verdad.
examples.en: Just tell the truth.

examples.es: Me llevaron al hospital de urgencias.
examples.en: They took me to the emergency hospital.

examples.es: Vivo en esta calle desde pequeño.
examples.en: I've lived on this street since I was small.

notes: Refers to the bathroom/toilet room as well as the act of bathing.

examples.es: ¿Dónde está el baño?
examples.en: Where is the bathroom?

examples.es: El rey firmó el decreto.
examples.en: The king signed the decree.

examples.es: ¿Tienes planes para el fin de semana?
examples.en: Do you have plans for the weekend?

examples.es: El control de calidad es esencial.
examples.en: Quality control is essential.

notes: Aire libre = outdoors; al aire = in the open; also means 'air conditioning' colloquially in Spain.

examples.es: Necesito salir a tomar un poco de aire.
examples.en: I need to go out and get some fresh air.

examples.es: El avión despegó a las doce.
examples.en: The plane took off at twelve.

examples.es: Tomamos el tren hasta Madrid.
examples.en: We took the train to Madrid.

examples.es: Lo condenaron a cinco años de cárcel.
examples.en: He was sentenced to five years in prison.

notes: En broma = jokingly; ¿Es una broma? = Are you kidding?

examples.es: Fue solo una broma, no te enfades.
examples.en: It was just a joke, don't get upset.

examples.es: Estás en peligro.
examples.en: You are in danger.

examples.es: La libertad de expresión es un derecho fundamental.
examples.en: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right.

examples.es: Ten la mente abierta.
examples.en: Keep an open mind.

notes: Short for fotografía. Despite ending in -o, it is feminine.

examples.es: ¿Me sacas una foto?
examples.en: Can you take a photo of me?

notes: Multiple meanings: countryside, field (agricultural or sports), and field (academic/professional).

examples.es: Pasamos el fin de semana en el campo.
examples.en: We spent the weekend in the countryside.

notes: Can mean the ground underfoot, the soil/earth, or a floor inside a building.

examples.es: El vaso cayó al suelo.
examples.en: The glass fell to the floor.

notes: Feminine noun that takes masculine article in singular (el alma) to avoid vowel clash.

examples.es: Lo siento en el alma.
examples.en: I feel it in my soul.

notes: Core verb with many uses: to carry/take (objects), to wear (clothes), to spend time doing something (llevo dos horas esperando = I've been waiting two hours).

examples.es: ¿Puedes llevar esto al coche?
examples.en: Can you take this to the car?

notes: To win (a competition) or to earn (money). Ganarse la vida = to make a living.

examples.es: Nuestro equipo ganó el partido.
examples.en: Our team won the match.

notes: Most common use: impersonal — me importa = it matters to me, no importa = it doesn't matter. Also means to import goods.

examples.es: No importa lo que digan.
examples.en: It doesn't matter what they say.

notes: Irregular: yo supongo (go-verb). Future/conditional stem: supondr-. Means to suppose, assume, or imply.

examples.es: Supongo que tienes razón.
examples.en: I suppose you're right.

notes: Stem-changing e→ie in stressed syllables (all persons except nosotros/vosotros in present). No me entiendes = You don't understand me.

examples.es: No entiendo lo que dices.
examples.en: I don't understand what you're saying.

notes: Regular -ar verb with spelling change c→qu before e (subjunctive). Most common use: ¿Qué significa…? = What does … mean?

examples.es: ¿Qué significa esta palabra?
examples.en: What does this word mean?

notes: Regular -ir verb but irregular past participle: abierto. Reflexive abrirse = to open up (emotionally or physically).

examples.es: Abre la puerta, por favor.
examples.en: Open the door, please.

notes: Stem-changing e→ie in stressed syllables. Common in both literal (close a door) and figurative (close a deal) senses.

examples.es: No olvides cerrar la ventana.
examples.en: Don't forget to close the window.

notes: Regular -ir verb but irregular past participle: escrito. Used for writing anything — letters, words, code, messages.

examples.es: Me escribe todos los días.
examples.en: She writes to me every day.

notes: The preterite has a y-form (leyó, leyeron) due to adjacent vowels, but present/future/conditional/subjunctive are regular.

examples.es: Me gusta leer antes de dormir.
examples.en: I like to read before sleeping.

notes: Stem-changing o→ue in stressed syllables. Recordar algo = to remember something; recordarle algo a alguien = to remind someone of something.

examples.es: No recuerdo dónde dejé las llaves.
examples.en: I don't remember where I left the keys.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Usually reflexive olvidarse de = to forget something. Transitive olvidar = to forget / leave behind.

examples.es: Olvidé mi teléfono en casa.
examples.en: I forgot my phone at home.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Preguntar por = to ask about/after someone. Distinguish from pedir (to ask for) and hacer una pregunta (to ask a question).

examples.es: Me preguntó si estaba bien.
examples.en: He asked me if I was okay.

notes: Highly versatile: quedar = to remain/be left; quedarse = to stay; quedar bien/mal = to look good/bad; quedar con alguien = to arrange to meet someone.

examples.es: Quedamos en el café a las cinco.
examples.en: We're meeting at the café at five.

notes: Regular -er verb. Literal: to put in/insert. Colloquial uses: meterse en = to get involved in; meterse con alguien = to pick on someone.

examples.es: Mete la ropa en la lavadora.
examples.en: Put the clothes in the washing machine.

notes: Regular -ar verb with c→qu before e. Sacar = to take out, get, extract, achieve (a grade), take (a photo). Sacar una foto = to take a photo.

examples.es: Saca el dinero del cajero.
examples.en: Take the money out of the ATM.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Intentar + infinitive = to try to do something. Synonym: tratar de.

examples.es: Intenté llamarte pero no contestaste.
examples.en: I tried to call you but you didn't answer.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Lograr + infinitive = to manage to / succeed in doing something. Implies actually achieving the goal, unlike intentar.

examples.es: Por fin logramos llegar a tiempo.
examples.en: We finally managed to arrive on time.

notes: Lowercase dios = a god (any deity). Uppercase Dios = God (monotheistic). ¡Dios mío! = My God! (common exclamation).

examples.es: ¡Dios mío, qué sorpresa!
examples.en: My God, what a surprise!

notes: Apocopated to algún before masculine singular nouns. Agrees: alguno/alguna/algunos/algunas. Used in affirmative contexts; en negatives use ninguno.

examples.es: ¿Tienes algún problema?
examples.en: Do you have any problem?

notes: Apocopated to ningún before masculine singular nouns. Agrees: ninguno/ninguna (rarely plural). Used in negative contexts; de ninguna manera = no way at all.

examples.es: No tengo ningún plan para hoy.
examples.en: I have no plan for today.

notes: Comparative and superlative of malo/mal (worse/worst). Invariable for gender; peores in plural. Lo peor = the worst thing.

examples.es: Lo peor ya ha pasado.
examples.en: The worst is already over.

notes: Adverb of place between aquí (here, near speaker) and allí/allá (there, far from both). Ahí mismo = right there.

examples.es: Ponlo ahí, encima de la mesa.
examples.en: Put it there, on top of the table.

notes: Directional adverb: forward, ahead. Also used as go-ahead: ¡Adelante! = Come in! / Go ahead! Más adelante = later / further ahead.

examples.es: ¡Adelante! La puerta está abierta.
examples.en: Come in! The door is open.

notes: Literary/formal conjunction meaning 'but'. No written accent — distinct from más (more). Rarely used in everyday speech; pero is the colloquial equivalent.

examples.es: Lo intenté, mas no pude.
examples.en: I tried, but I couldn't.

notes: Prepositional pronoun, contraction of con + ti (you). Always with con — never *con ti. Cf. conmigo (with me), consigo (with him/herself).

examples.es: Quiero hablar contigo.
examples.en: I want to talk with you.

notes: Neuter personal pronoun referring to a concept, idea, or situation (never a physical noun). Por ello = for that reason. Rarely used as subject; usually implied.

examples.es: No quiero hablar de ello.
examples.en: I don't want to talk about it.

notes: Regular -er verb. Aprender a + infinitive = to learn to do something.

examples.es: Quiero aprender a tocar la guitarra.
examples.en: I want to learn to play the guitar.

notes: Regular -er verb. Used for drinking any liquid. Cf. tomar, which is broader (to have food or drink).

examples.es: ¿Qué quieres beber?
examples.en: What do you want to drink?

notes: Regular -er verb. Literal: to run. Also: to rush, to move quickly. Correrse = to move over.

examples.es: Corro todos los días por el parque.
examples.en: I run in the park every day.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Tratar de + inf = to try to; tratar a alguien = to treat/deal with someone; tratarse de = to be about.

examples.es: Este libro trata de la guerra.
examples.en: This book is about the war.

notes: Regular -er verb. Se vende = for sale. Venderse = to sell out (ideologically) or be sold.

examples.es: Venden frutas frescas en ese mercado.
examples.en: They sell fresh fruit at that market.

notes: Regular -ar verb. More literary/intense than querer for expressing love. Te amo is common in Latin America; Spain more often uses te quiero.

examples.es: Te amo con todo mi corazón.
examples.en: I love you with all my heart.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Gritar a alguien = to shout at someone.

examples.es: No me grites, por favor.
examples.en: Please don't shout at me.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Llorar de alegría = to cry with joy. Commonly used both transitively and intransitively.

examples.es: El bebé llora cuando tiene hambre.
examples.en: The baby cries when it's hungry.

notes: Irregular yo form: nazco (c→zc). Nacer en = to be born in. Usually used in past tense in practice (nació = he/she was born).

examples.es: Nació en Buenos Aires en 1985.
examples.en: She was born in Buenos Aires in 1985.

notes: Regular -ar verb with spelling change c→qu before e (subjunctive/preterite). Explicar algo a alguien = to explain something to someone.

examples.es: ¿Me puedes explicar cómo funciona?
examples.en: Can you explain to me how it works?

notes: Stem-changing o→ue in stressed syllables. Mostrar algo a alguien = to show something to someone.

examples.es: Déjame mostrarte algo interesante.
examples.en: Let me show you something interesting.

notes: Regular -ar verb with accent on the u in stressed forms (continúo, continúas, etc.) to mark it as a diphthong-breaking vowel.

examples.es: Por favor, continúa con tu historia.
examples.en: Please continue with your story.

notes: Stem-changing o→ue. Three main uses: (1) to taste/try (food), (2) to test/try out, (3) to prove. Probarse = to try on (clothing).

examples.es: ¿Puedo probar ese postre?
examples.en: Can I try that dessert?

notes: Regular -ar verb. Often impersonal like gustar: me falta dinero = I'm short of money. Faltar a = to miss/skip (a class, a promise).

examples.es: Nos falta tiempo para terminar.
examples.en: We don't have enough time to finish.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Neutral word for walking; andar is a common synonym with broader uses.

examples.es: Caminamos hasta la plaza.
examples.en: We walked to the square.

notes: Irregular yo form: crezco (c→zc). Refers to physical or figurative growth.

examples.es: Los niños crecen muy rápido.
examples.en: Children grow up very fast.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Two core meanings: (1) to teach (a subject or skill), (2) to show (something to someone).

examples.es: Ella enseña matemáticas en el colegio.
examples.en: She teaches mathematics at school.

notes: Regular -ir verb. Sufrir de = to suffer from (an illness). Also used for enduring hardship.

examples.es: No quiero que sufras por mi culpa.
examples.en: I don't want you to suffer because of me.

notes: Regular -ir verb, usually impersonal: ocurre que = it happens that; ¿qué ocurre? = what's happening? Synonym: pasar, suceder.

examples.es: ¿Sabes lo que ocurrió anoche?
examples.en: Do you know what happened last night?

examples.es: ¿Cuál es tu color favorito?
examples.en: What is your favourite colour?

examples.es: ¿Cuánto es el precio de entrada?
examples.en: How much is the entry price?

notes: Note irregular plural spelling: millón → millones. When followed by a noun: un millón de personas (de is required).

examples.es: Hay más de un millón de personas en esa ciudad.
examples.en: There are more than a million people in that city.

examples.es: Tomo café con leche por las mañanas.
examples.en: I have coffee with milk in the mornings.

notes: Note: vino is also the preterite 3rd-person singular of venir (he/she came) — context distinguishes the two.

examples.es: Pidieron una botella de vino tinto.
examples.en: They ordered a bottle of red wine.

examples.es: ¿Me pones una cerveza fría, por favor?
examples.en: Can you get me a cold beer, please?

notes: Literal: fire, flame. Also used idiomatically: pedir fuego = to ask for a light (cigarette); fuegos artificiales = fireworks.

examples.es: El fuego se extendió rápidamente.
examples.en: The fire spread quickly.

notes: Gender affects meaning: el orden = order (arrangement, sequence); la orden = command/order (instruction). Plural órdenes for both.

examples.es: Sigue las órdenes del médico.
examples.en: Follow the doctor's orders.

notes: Multiple meanings: back (of a room), bottom (of a container), background (of an image), fund (financial). Al fondo = at the back.

examples.es: El baño está al fondo del pasillo.
examples.en: The bathroom is at the end of the corridor.

notes: As feminine noun: forehead. As masculine noun: front (military, political, weather). Frente a = opposite/in front of (preposition).

examples.es: El hotel está justo enfrente de la estación.
examples.en: The hotel is right opposite the station.

notes: As noun: sense (one of the five senses), meaning, direction. As adjective: heartfelt. Tiene sentido = it makes sense; sin sentido = meaningless.

examples.es: Lo que dices no tiene ningún sentido.
examples.en: What you're saying makes no sense.

examples.es: El precio es veinte dólares.
examples.en: The price is twenty dollars.

notes: Opposite of verdad. Decir una mentira = to tell a lie. ¡Mentira! = That's a lie! / No way!

examples.es: No soporto las mentiras.
examples.en: I can't stand lies.

examples.es: Tenemos que encontrar una solución rápida.
examples.en: We need to find a quick solution.

notes: Usually plural las noticias = the news (broadcast). Una noticia = a piece of news. False friend: notice in English ≠ noticia.

examples.es: ¿Has oído las últimas noticias?
examples.en: Have you heard the latest news?

notes: Three main meanings: letter (mail), playing card, menu (in a restaurant). Carta de presentación = cover letter.

examples.es: El camarero nos trajo la carta.
examples.en: The waiter brought us the menu.

notes: As noun (feminine): list. As adjective (lista/listo): clever, ready. ¿Estás listo? = Are you ready?

examples.es: Haz una lista de todo lo que necesitas.
examples.en: Make a list of everything you need.

notes: Primary meaning: room (any room). Also: quarter (1/4). Son las tres y cuarto = it's quarter past three.

examples.es: Mi cuarto es pequeño pero cómodo.
examples.en: My room is small but comfortable.

notes: Meanings: step (physical), pace, pass (mountain pass), crossing (zebra crossing). Paso a paso = step by step. Dar un paso = to take a step.

examples.es: Da un paso hacia adelante.
examples.en: Take a step forward.

notes: Meanings: lack, absence, fault, foul (sport). Hacer falta = to be needed. Sin falta = without fail.

examples.es: Aquí hace falta más luz.
examples.en: More light is needed here.

notes: Relative pronoun. Usually preceded by article: el cual, la cual, los cuales, las cuales — used for added clarity or in formal registers. Cuál (with accent) is interrogative.

examples.es: El informe, el cual presentamos ayer, fue aprobado.
examples.en: The report, which we presented yesterday, was approved.

notes: Adverb of place meaning behind. Used with de: detrás de la puerta = behind the door.

examples.es: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.en: The garden is behind the house.

notes: Almost always used as acerca de = about, regarding, concerning. Rarely used without de.

examples.es: Hablamos acerca del proyecto.
examples.en: We talked about the project.

notes: Exclamatory use of the 3rd-person present of bastar (to be enough). ¡Basta ya! = That's enough! / Stop it! Often used to end an argument.

examples.es: ¡Basta! No quiero escuchar más.
examples.en: Enough! I don't want to hear any more.

notes: Fixed adverb meaning last night. The exact Spanish counterpart of 'last night'; esta noche = tonight.

examples.es: Anoche no pude dormir.
examples.en: Last night I couldn't sleep.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Used for machines, plans, relationships: ¿Funciona? = Does it work? No funciona = It's broken.

examples.es: El ascensor no funciona hoy.
examples.en: The lift isn't working today.

notes: Regular -ar verb. The noun el odio = hatred uses the same yo-form spelling.

examples.es: Odio levantarme temprano.
examples.en: I hate getting up early.

notes: Regular -er verb. Usually impersonal: sucede que… = it happens that… ¿Qué sucede? = What's happening? Synonym: pasar, ocurrir.

examples.es: ¿Sabes lo que sucedió aquí?
examples.en: Do you know what happened here?

notes: Un par de = a couple of / a pair of. As adjective (invariable): even number (número par). De par en par = wide open.

examples.es: Dame un par de minutos.
examples.en: Give me a couple of minutes.

notes: Gender-common (el/la agente). Covers law enforcement officer, real-estate agent, travel agent, and grammatical agent.

examples.es: El agente le pidió la documentación.
examples.en: The officer asked him for his documents.

notes: Broad word for any matter, affair, or subject. Asuntos exteriores = foreign affairs. No es asunto tuyo = It's none of your business.

examples.es: Hay un asunto urgente que tratar.
examples.en: There is an urgent matter to deal with.

notes: Used for text messages, voicemails, and broader communications. Dejar un mensaje = to leave a message.

examples.es: Te mandé un mensaje pero no respondiste.
examples.en: I sent you a message but you didn't reply.

notes: Hacer daño = to hurt/harm. Hacerse daño = to hurt oneself. Also used in legal/insurance contexts: daños y perjuicios = damages.

examples.es: El granizo causó daños en los cultivos.
examples.en: The hail caused damage to the crops.

notes: Girlfriend or bride (at a wedding). Novio = boyfriend/groom. The word does not distinguish casual dating from serious relationship.

examples.es: Lleva tres años con su novia.
examples.en: He's been with his girlfriend for three years.

notes: Taste (sense) or pleasure. Mucho gusto = nice to meet you. Con mucho gusto = with pleasure. A gusto = comfortable/at ease.

examples.es: Mucho gusto en conocerte.
examples.en: Nice to meet you.

notes: Three main meanings: appointment (medical/business), date (romantic), quotation. Tener una cita = to have an appointment or a date.

examples.es: Tengo una cita con el médico a las tres.
examples.en: I have a doctor's appointment at three.

notes: As noun: secret. As adjective: secret/secretive (agente secreto). Guardar un secreto = to keep a secret. En secreto = in secret.

examples.es: Prometió guardar el secreto.
examples.en: He promised to keep the secret.

notes: Core meanings: pity/shame (¡Qué pena! = What a shame!), sorrow/grief, and penalty/punishment (pena de muerte = death penalty).

examples.es: ¡Qué pena que no puedas venir!
examples.en: What a shame you can't come!

examples.es: La situación es más grave de lo que pensaba.
examples.en: The situation is more serious than I thought.

examples.es: Reservamos un hotel cerca de la playa.
examples.en: We booked a hotel near the beach.

notes: Masculine despite -a ending. Covers TV show, computer program, schedule, and political programme.

examples.es: ¿Qué programa de televisión te gusta más?
examples.en: Which TV show do you like most?

examples.es: Estudié Medicina en la universidad.
examples.en: I studied Medicine at university.

notes: Lowercase iglesia = any church building. Uppercase Iglesia = the institution (la Iglesia Católica).

examples.es: La boda fue en una iglesia pequeña.
examples.en: The wedding was in a small church.

notes: Two key meanings: (1) apartment/flat (Spain), (2) floor/storey of a building. Latin America prefers apartamento or departamento for sense 1.

examples.es: Vivo en un piso en el centro de la ciudad.
examples.en: I live in a flat in the city centre.

notes: Both the room (kitchen) and the activity (cooking/cuisine). Cocina española = Spanish cuisine.

examples.es: Preparó una cena increíble en la cocina.
examples.en: She prepared an incredible dinner in the kitchen.

notes: Lowercase luna = the moon or any moon. Uppercase Luna = Earth's moon (proper noun). Luna de miel = honeymoon.

examples.es: Esta noche hay luna llena.
examples.en: There's a full moon tonight.

notes: Usually masculine (el mar) in standard usage, but feminine (la mar) in poetry and some regional/fixed expressions (a la mar = out to sea).

examples.es: Pasamos las vacaciones junto al mar.
examples.en: We spent the holidays by the sea.

notes: Por ejemplo = for example (common discourse marker). Dar un ejemplo = to give an example.

examples.es: Por ejemplo, puedes usar este método.
examples.en: For example, you can use this method.

notes: Both physical window and computer window (la ventana del navegador).

examples.es: Abre la ventana, hace calor.
examples.en: Open the window, it's hot.

notes: Both astronomical star and celebrity/star (una estrella de cine = a film star). Estrella de mar = starfish.

examples.es: Podemos ver las estrellas desde aquí.
examples.en: We can see the stars from here.

notes: Invariable for gender. Ponerse triste = to become sad. Qué triste = how sad.

examples.es: Se puso triste cuando escuchó la noticia.
examples.en: She became sad when she heard the news.

notes: Literal: eye. Also used as a warning exclamation: ¡Ojo! = Watch out! / Be careful! Ojear = to skim/glance at.

examples.es: Tiene los ojos muy claros.
examples.en: She has very light eyes.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: extraño/extraña/extraños/extrañas. Also used as a noun (un extraño = a stranger). Qué extraño = how strange.

examples.es: Hay algo extraño en esa casa.
examples.en: There's something strange about that house.

notes: Two meanings: (1) strange/odd, (2) rare/uncommon. Qué raro = how odd/strange. Rara vez = rarely.

examples.es: Qué raro, no contesta el teléfono.
examples.en: How strange, he's not answering the phone.

notes: As adjective: general, overall, widespread. As noun (el general): military general. En general = in general, generally.

examples.es: En general, estoy de acuerdo contigo.
examples.en: In general, I agree with you.

notes: As adjective: straight, upright, right (direction). As noun (el derecho): law (the subject) or a right (legal/moral). Todo recto = straight ahead.

examples.es: Tienes derecho a saber la verdad.
examples.en: You have the right to know the truth.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Describes something or someone as fun/entertaining. Qué divertido = how fun! Divertirse = to have fun.

examples.es: Fue una noche muy divertida.
examples.en: It was a very fun night.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Means own (su propia casa = his own house), proper/appropriate, or characteristic of. Lo propio = the same / likewise.

examples.es: Tiene su propio estilo.
examples.en: She has her own style.

notes: Before noun: pitiful/unfortunate (el pobre hombre = the poor man). After noun: financially poor (una familia pobre). As noun: a poor person.

examples.es: El pobre chico no sabía qué hacer.
examples.en: The poor guy didn't know what to do.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: negro/negra/negros/negras. Colour black. As noun: Black person. Mercado negro = black market.

examples.es: Quiero el café negro, sin azúcar.
examples.en: I want black coffee, no sugar.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Colloquial and can be mild or harsh depending on tone. As noun: a fool/idiot.

examples.es: No seas tonto, claro que puedes.
examples.en: Don't be silly, of course you can.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Two meanings: next (in sequence) and near/nearby (proximity). La próxima vez = next time.

examples.es: Nos vemos la próxima semana.
examples.en: See you next week.

notes: Adverb of place: on top, above, overhead. With de: encima de = on top of. Colloquial: on top of that, to make matters worse.

examples.es: El libro está encima de la mesa.
examples.en: The book is on top of the table.

notes: As adverb: around, surrounding. With de: alrededor de = around/approximately. A su alrededor = around him/her.

examples.es: Había gente alrededor del escenario.
examples.en: There were people around the stage.

notes: Always with article: los/las demás = the others/the rest. Lo demás = the rest (of it). Invariable for gender; takes plural verb.

examples.es: Los demás ya se han ido.
examples.en: The others have already left.

notes: Formal/written alternative to los dos. Agrees in gender: ambos/ambas. Always refers to two things or people already mentioned.

examples.es: Ambos candidatos tienen buenas ideas.
examples.en: Both candidates have good ideas.

notes: Adverb (invariable) meaning early. As adjective (agrees: temprano/temprana) it is less common. Opposite: tarde.

examples.es: Mañana tengo que levantarme temprano.
examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.

notes: Feminine noun. Prestar atención = to pay attention. ¡Atención! = Attention! / Watch out! Used also in customer service context.

examples.es: Presta atención a lo que te digo.
examples.en: Pay attention to what I'm telling you.

notes: Masculine noun. Foot (body part). De pie = standing up. A pie = on foot. Al pie de la letra = to the letter (exactly).

examples.es: Me duele el pie derecho.
examples.en: My right foot hurts.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Salvar la vida = to save someone's life. Salvarse = to survive/escape.

examples.es: El médico le salvó la vida.
examples.en: The doctor saved his life.

notes: Regular -ar verb with accent shift: confío, confías, confía (stress on í). Confiar en = to trust in/rely on. Confiar algo a alguien = to entrust something to someone.

examples.es: Confío en ti completamente.
examples.en: I trust you completely.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Luchar contra = to fight against. Luchar por = to fight for. Covers both physical combat and figurative struggle.

examples.es: Hay que luchar por lo que uno quiere.
examples.en: You have to fight for what you want.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Three common meanings: (1) to fix/repair, (2) to tidy/sort out, (3) to arrange. Arreglarse = to get ready/sort oneself out.

examples.es: ¿Puedes arreglar el grifo que gotea?
examples.en: Can you fix the leaking tap?

notes: Regular -ar verb. Robar algo a alguien = to steal something from someone. Also used colloquially for overcharging (¡Me están robando! = They're robbing me!).

examples.es: Le robaron la cartera en el metro.
examples.en: His wallet was stolen on the metro.

notes: Regular -er verb but irregular past participle: roto. Romperse = to break/snap (reflexive). Romper con alguien = to break up with someone.

examples.es: Se me rompió el teléfono.
examples.en: My phone broke.

notes: Regular -ar verb with accent shift on stressed í: envío, envías, envía, enviáis (no accent), envían.

examples.es: Te enviaré el documento por correo.
examples.en: I'll send you the document by email.

notes: Regular -ir verb. Recibir a alguien = to receive/welcome someone. Recibir noticias = to get news.

examples.es: Recibí tu mensaje esta mañana.
examples.en: I received your message this morning.

notes: Regular -er verb with spelling change g→j before a/o (protejo, proteja). Protegerse de = to protect oneself from.

examples.es: Su misión es proteger a los ciudadanos.
examples.en: His mission is to protect the citizens.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Limpiar la casa = to clean the house. Also figurative: limpiar la imagen = to clean up one's image.

examples.es: Voy a limpiar la cocina después de cenar.
examples.en: I'm going to clean the kitchen after dinner.

notes: Irregular -ir verb with y insertion: destruyo, destruyes, destruye, destruimos, destruís, destruyen. Subjunctive: destruya…

examples.es: El fuego destruyó el edificio por completo.
examples.en: The fire completely destroyed the building.

notes: Stem-changing e→ie in stressed syllables. Also e→i in gerund (mintiendo) and 3rd-person preterite (mintió, mintieron) — but we omit preterite here.

examples.es: No me gusta que me mientan.
examples.en: I don't like people lying to me.

notes: General word for any boat or ship. Barco de vela = sailing boat. Barco de vapor = steamship.

examples.es: El barco salió del puerto al amanecer.
examples.en: The ship left the port at dawn.

notes: The common table salt. Sales (plural) = salts (chemistry, bath salts). Echar sal = to add salt.

examples.es: Pon un poco de sal a la pasta.
examples.en: Add a little salt to the pasta.

notes: As noun: dress (clothing). As adjective (vestido/a): dressed. Vestido de noche = evening dress.

examples.es: Llevaba un vestido rojo en la fiesta.
examples.en: She was wearing a red dress at the party.

notes: Carne de res = beef. Carne de cerdo = pork. Carne de pollo = chicken. Also the word for flesh (physical tissue).

examples.es: No como carne, soy vegetariano.
examples.en: I don't eat meat, I'm vegetarian.

notes: Gender-common: el/la cliente. Covers customer (in a shop), client (professional), and patron.

examples.es: El cliente siempre tiene razón.
examples.en: The customer is always right.

notes: Three meanings: (1) trial/court case, (2) judgement/opinion, (3) good sense/sanity. Perder el juicio = to lose one's mind.

examples.es: El juicio comenzará la próxima semana.
examples.en: The trial will begin next week.

notes: Key (door, car). Llave inglesa = wrench/spanner. Llave maestra = master key. Also: tap/faucet in some Latin American countries.

examples.es: ¿Has visto mis llaves del coche?
examples.en: Have you seen my car keys?

notes: The back of the body. De espaldas = with one's back turned. Dar la espalda a alguien = to turn one's back on someone.

examples.es: Me duele mucho la espalda.
examples.en: My back hurts a lot.

notes: Broad term: work of art, literary work, theatrical play, construction/building works. En obras = under construction.

examples.es: Es una obra maestra de la literatura española.
examples.en: It's a masterpiece of Spanish literature.

examples.es: El río Amazonas es el más largo del mundo.
examples.en: The Amazon River is the longest in the world.

notes: Neck (body part). Also the collar of a garment. Cuello de botella = bottleneck.

examples.es: Me duele el cuello de estar mirando el móvil.
examples.en: My neck hurts from looking at my phone.

notes: Arm (body part). En brazos = in (someone's) arms. A brazo partido = tooth and nail (fighting hard).

examples.es: Se rompió el brazo jugando al fútbol.
examples.en: He broke his arm playing football.

notes: A forest or wood. Bosque tropical = rainforest. Distinguishable from selva (dense jungle) and arboleda (grove).

examples.es: Dimos un paseo por el bosque.
examples.en: We went for a walk in the forest.

notes: Covers surgical operation, military operation, and mathematical operation. Sala de operaciones = operating theatre.

examples.es: La operación duró más de cuatro horas.
examples.en: The operation lasted more than four hours.

notes: Business company or firm. Also 'enterprise' in the sense of a bold undertaking. Empresario/a = businessman/woman.

examples.es: Trabaja en una empresa de tecnología.
examples.en: She works at a technology company.

notes: Dar un beso = to give a kiss. Un beso (at the end of messages) = Kisses / Love. Beso en la mejilla = kiss on the cheek.

examples.es: Le dio un beso de buenas noches.
examples.en: She gave him a goodnight kiss.

notes: Truck or lorry. In Mexico, camión also means bus (intercity or city bus).

examples.es: Un camión bloqueó la carretera.
examples.en: A truck blocked the road.

notes: Noise or sound (usually unwanted). Hacer ruido = to make noise. Sin ruido = silently.

examples.es: Los vecinos hacen mucho ruido por las noches.
examples.en: The neighbours make a lot of noise at night.

notes: Bread. Also a loaf of bread. Pan de molde = sliced bread. Ganarse el pan = to earn one's bread/living.

examples.es: Compra un par de barras de pan.
examples.en: Buy a couple of baguettes.

notes: Project or plan. Proyecto de ley = bill (legislative). En proyecto = planned/in the pipeline.

examples.es: Estamos trabajando en un proyecto muy interesante.
examples.en: We're working on a very interesting project.

notes: Interior wall of a building. Cf. muro (exterior/structural wall) and valla (fence). Entre estas cuatro paredes = within these four walls.

examples.es: Colgó el cuadro en la pared.
examples.en: He hung the picture on the wall.

notes: Chair. Sillón = armchair. Silla de ruedas = wheelchair. Silla alta = high chair.

examples.es: Siéntate en esa silla, por favor.
examples.en: Sit in that chair, please.

notes: Illness or disease. Enfermedad crónica = chronic illness. Enfermedad contagiosa = contagious disease.

examples.es: Se recuperó de su enfermedad rápidamente.
examples.en: She recovered from her illness quickly.

notes: Wind. Hace viento = it's windy. A los cuatro vientos = to the four winds (everywhere). Molino de viento = windmill.

examples.es: Hace mucho viento hoy.
examples.en: It's very windy today.

notes: Leg (body part from hip to foot). Cf. pie (foot) and rodilla (knee). Estirar las piernas = to stretch one's legs.

examples.es: Se rompió la pierna en el accidente.
examples.en: She broke her leg in the accident.

notes: Note irregular plural: nariz → narices. Sonarse la nariz = to blow one's nose. Meter las narices = to stick one's nose in.

examples.es: Me pica la nariz.
examples.en: My nose is itchy.

notes: Standard word for bus (city or intercity). Shortened to bus in informal use. In Latin America often replaced by camión, colectivo, micro, or ómnibus depending on region.

examples.es: Tomamos el autobús hasta el centro.
examples.en: We took the bus to the city centre.

notes: Invariable for gender (inteligente for both masc and fem). Agrees in number: inteligentes. Ser inteligente = to be intelligent (permanent trait).

examples.es: Es la persona más inteligente que conozco.
examples.en: She's the most intelligent person I know.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: lleno/llena/llenos/llenas. Estar lleno = to be full (of food or of a container). Lleno de = full of.

examples.es: El teatro estaba lleno de gente.
examples.en: The theatre was full of people.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Estar enfermo/a = to be ill (current state). Also used as a noun: el enfermo/la enferma = the patient/sick person.

examples.es: No pude ir a trabajar porque estaba enfermo.
examples.en: I couldn't go to work because I was ill.

notes: Adjective invariable for gender (paciente/pacientes). Also used as a noun: el/la paciente = the patient (medical).

examples.es: Hay que ser paciente; las cosas llevan tiempo.
examples.en: You have to be patient; things take time.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: rico/rica/ricos/ricas. Two core meanings: (1) wealthy/rich, (2) delicious (food). ¡Qué rico! = How delicious!

examples.es: Este pastel está riquísimo.
examples.en: This cake is absolutely delicious.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Estar cansado/a = to be tired (state). Cansarse = to get tired. Also: cansado de = tired of (fed up with).

examples.es: Estoy muy cansada después del viaje.
examples.en: I'm very tired after the journey.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Estar nervioso/a = to be nervous. Ponerse nervioso = to get nervous. System nervioso = nervous system.

examples.es: Siempre me pongo nervioso antes de los exámenes.
examples.en: I always get nervous before exams.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Estar orgulloso de = to be proud of. Can carry a negative connotation of arrogance in some contexts.

examples.es: Estoy muy orgullosa de mis hijos.
examples.en: I'm very proud of my children.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: limpio/limpia/limpios/limpias. Opposite: sucio. Estar limpio = to be clean. Tener las manos limpias = to have clean hands (be innocent).

examples.es: Deja el baño limpio después de usarlo.
examples.en: Leave the bathroom clean after using it.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Parar de + inf = to stop doing something. Pararse = to stop (reflexive). Also: to stand up (Latin America).

examples.es: Para el coche aquí, por favor.
examples.en: Stop the car here, please.

notes: Regular -ar with c→qu before e. Three main meanings: (1) to touch, (2) to play an instrument, (3) to be someone's turn — me toca = it's my turn.

examples.es: ¿Tocas algún instrumento?
examples.en: Do you play any instrument?

notes: Regular -ir verb. Subir = to go up, climb, rise, upload. Subirse a = to get on/into (a vehicle). Subir el volumen = to turn up the volume.

examples.es: Sube las escaleras con cuidado.
examples.en: Go up the stairs carefully.

notes: Stem-changing o→ue. Literal: to fly (birds, planes). Figurative: to fly by (time). Volar por los aires = to blow up/explode.

examples.es: El avión vuela a diez mil metros de altura.
examples.en: The plane flies at ten thousand metres altitude.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Bajar = to go down, lower, descend, download. Bajarse de = to get off (a vehicle). Bajar el volumen = to turn down the volume.

examples.es: Baja la voz, que están durmiendo.
examples.en: Lower your voice, they're sleeping.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Aceptar una oferta = to accept an offer. Aceptar que = to accept/acknowledge that.

examples.es: Aceptaron las condiciones del contrato.
examples.en: They accepted the terms of the contract.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Imaginarse = to imagine/picture (reflexive). ¡Imagínate! = Just imagine! / Can you believe it!

examples.es: Imagina que puedes volar.
examples.en: Imagine you can fly.

notes: Regular -ir verb. Decidir + inf = to decide to do something. Decidirse a = to make up one's mind to.

examples.es: ¿Ya has decidido qué vas a estudiar?
examples.en: Have you already decided what you're going to study?

notes: Regular -ar verb. Cortarse = to cut oneself, or to be cut off (phone call). Cortar con alguien = to break up with someone.

examples.es: Corta el pan en rodajas.
examples.en: Cut the bread into slices.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Nadar a braza/crol/espalda = to swim breaststroke/crawl/backstroke.

examples.es: Aprendí a nadar cuando era niño.
examples.en: I learned to swim when I was a child.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Preparar la comida = to prepare a meal. Prepararse para = to prepare oneself for.

examples.es: Voy a preparar la cena.
examples.en: I'm going to prepare dinner.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Distinguishable from hacer la comida (to make food) — cocinar implies culinary skill or effort.

examples.es: Me encanta cocinar para mis amigos.
examples.en: I love cooking for my friends.

notes: Sala de estar = living room. Sala de espera = waiting room. Sala de cine = cinema screen/theatre.

examples.es: Nos reunimos todos en la sala de estar.
examples.en: We all gathered in the living room.

notes: Camera (photo/video). Also chamber (legislative body): Cámara de Diputados. Cámara de fotos = still camera; cámara de vídeo = video camera.

examples.es: Olvidé la cámara en el hotel.
examples.en: I forgot the camera at the hotel.

notes: Primary school teacher or master of a craft/art. La maestra = female teacher. Also used as a respectful address: ¡Maestro!

examples.es: El maestro explicó la lección con paciencia.
examples.en: The teacher explained the lesson patiently.

notes: Horse. A caballo = on horseback. Caballo de batalla = pet subject/hobby horse. Also the knight piece in chess.

examples.es: Montó a caballo por primera vez.
examples.en: She rode a horse for the first time.

notes: Note the accent to distinguish from te (pronoun). Té con leche = tea with milk. Té verde/negro = green/black tea.

examples.es: ¿Te apetece una taza de té?
examples.en: Would you like a cup of tea?

notes: In Spain usually feminine (la radio). In Latin America often masculine (el radio). El radio also means radius in geometry.

examples.es: Escucho la radio mientras conduzco.
examples.en: I listen to the radio while I drive.

notes: Gender-common: el juez / la jueza (also la juez). Note plural: jueces. Juez de paz = justice of the peace.

examples.es: El juez dictó la sentencia.
examples.en: The judge delivered the verdict.

notes: Gender-common: el/la soldado. Rank-and-file soldier. Soldado raso = private (lowest military rank).

examples.es: Los soldados regresaron a casa después de la misión.
examples.en: The soldiers returned home after the mission.

examples.es: Hay un árbol muy alto en el jardín.
examples.en: There's a very tall tree in the garden.

notes: La gata = female cat. Also: car jack (tool). Jugar al gato y al ratón = to play cat and mouse.

examples.es: Tenemos dos gatos en casa.
examples.en: We have two cats at home.

notes: Shortened informally to tele. Televisión de pantalla plana = flat-screen TV. Ver la televisión = to watch television.

examples.es: Pasamos la tarde viendo la televisión.
examples.en: We spent the afternoon watching television.

examples.es: Necesito un cuchillo para cortar la carne.
examples.en: I need a knife to cut the meat.

notes: Also used informally to mean a brute or rough person.

examples.es: Los niños aprenden los nombres de los animales.
examples.en: Children learn the names of animals.

notes: A look, gaze, or glance. Echar una mirada = to take a look. Una mirada perdida = a vacant stare.

examples.es: Me lanzó una mirada de sorpresa.
examples.en: She gave me a surprised look.

notes: A garden (cultivated outdoor space). Jardín de infancia/infantil = kindergarten.

examples.es: Las flores del jardín huelen muy bien.
examples.en: The flowers in the garden smell lovely.

notes: Chicken (the bird or the meat). Pollo asado = roast chicken. Pechuga de pollo = chicken breast.

examples.es: Vamos a cenar pollo asado esta noche.
examples.en: We're having roast chicken for dinner tonight.

notes: Short story or tale. Cuento de hadas = fairy tale. No me vengas con cuentos = don't give me excuses/tall tales.

examples.es: Le leía un cuento antes de dormir.
examples.en: He read her a story before bed.

examples.es: ¿Quieres más queso en la pizza?
examples.en: Do you want more cheese on the pizza?

notes: Both the artwork (a painting) and the substance (paint). Pintura al óleo = oil painting. Pintura de paredes = wall paint.

examples.es: Tiene una colección de pinturas muy valiosas.
examples.en: He has a very valuable collection of paintings.

notes: Plate/dish (the object). Also a dish/course of a meal: primer plato = starter, plato principal = main course. Lavar los platos = to do the dishes.

examples.es: El plato principal fue un filete a la plancha.
examples.en: The main course was a grilled steak.

notes: A promise. Cumplir una promesa = to keep a promise. Romper una promesa = to break a promise.

examples.es: Cumplió su promesa y volvió.
examples.en: He kept his promise and came back.

notes: A smile. Esbozar una sonrisa = to manage a smile. Sonrisa de oreja a oreja = ear-to-ear grin.

examples.es: Su sonrisa ilumina la habitación.
examples.en: Her smile lights up the room.

notes: Cup or mug. Una taza de café = a cup of coffee. Distinct from vaso (a glass/tumbler without a handle).

examples.es: ¿Me preparas una taza de té?
examples.en: Can you make me a cup of tea?

notes: A drinking glass (tumbler, no handle). Distinct from copa (stemmed glass for wine) and taza (cup with handle).

examples.es: ¿Me das un vaso de agua, por favor?
examples.en: Can you give me a glass of water, please?

notes: A nightmare. Tener una pesadilla = to have a nightmare. Also used figuratively: fue una pesadilla = it was a nightmare.

examples.es: Tuve una pesadilla horrible anoche.
examples.en: I had a horrible nightmare last night.

notes: Gender-common: el/la estudiante. Covers school pupils and university students.

examples.es: Los estudiantes presentaron sus proyectos.
examples.en: The students presented their projects.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: vivo/viva/vivos/vivas. Estar vivo = to be alive. Also: vivid, bright (colour), clever/sharp (person).

examples.es: Afortunadamente, todos salieron vivos del accidente.
examples.en: Fortunately, everyone came out of the accident alive.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Past participle of perder used as adjective. Estar perdido = to be lost. Also: hopeless case.

examples.es: Estoy completamente perdido en esta ciudad.
examples.en: I'm completely lost in this city.

notes: Invariable for gender (dulce for masc and fem). Agrees in number: dulces. Used for taste (sweet) and personality (gentle/sweet).

examples.es: Este postre está demasiado dulce para mi gusto.
examples.en: This dessert is too sweet for my taste.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: frío/fría/fríos/frías. Tener frío = to feel cold (person). Hacer frío = to be cold (weather). Estar frío = to be cold (object).

examples.es: El agua está muy fría hoy.
examples.en: The water is very cold today.

notes: Invariable for gender (caliente). Agrees in number: calientes. Estar caliente = to be hot (object). Hacer calor = to be hot (weather) — note: caliente ≠ calor.

examples.es: Cuidado, el café está muy caliente.
examples.en: Careful, the coffee is very hot.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Estar ocupado/a = to be busy (person) or occupied (seat/toilet). Tener la línea ocupada = the line is busy.

examples.es: Lo siento, estoy muy ocupada ahora mismo.
examples.en: Sorry, I'm very busy right now.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Past participle of herir used as adjective. Estar herido/a = to be injured/wounded. Also used as a noun: el/la herido/a = the injured person.

examples.es: Había tres personas heridas en el accidente.
examples.en: There were three people injured in the accident.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: oscuro/oscura/oscuros/oscuras. A oscuras = in the dark. Colores oscuros = dark colours.

examples.es: La habitación estaba completamente oscura.
examples.en: The room was completely dark.

notes: Invariable for gender (débil). Agrees in number: débiles. Punto débil = weak point.

examples.es: Se sentía débil después de la enfermedad.
examples.en: She felt weak after the illness.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Past participle of asustar used as adjective. Estar asustado/a = to be scared. Asustar = to frighten.

examples.es: El niño estaba asustado por la tormenta.
examples.en: The child was scared by the storm.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: sucio/sucia/sucios/sucias. Opposite: limpio. Juego sucio = foul play.

examples.es: Tienes las manos sucias, ve a lavártelas.
examples.en: Your hands are dirty, go and wash them.

notes: Agrees in gender/number: vacío/vacía/vacíos/vacías. Note the accent. Also used as a noun: el vacío = the void/emptiness.

examples.es: El frigorífico está casi vacío.
examples.en: The fridge is almost empty.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Two uses: estar aburrido/a = to be bored (person); ser aburrido/a = to be boring (thing/person). Aburrir = to bore.

examples.es: Me aburro mucho en las reuniones largas.
examples.en: I get really bored in long meetings.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. More common in Latin America; Spain prefers enfadado. Estar enojado/a con alguien = to be angry with someone.

examples.es: Está muy enojado con su hermano.
examples.en: He's very angry with his brother.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Bailar salsa/tango/flamenco = to dance salsa/tango/flamenco. Sacar a bailar a alguien = to ask someone to dance.

examples.es: ¿Quieres bailar conmigo?
examples.en: Do you want to dance with me?

notes: Regular -ar verb. Escaparse = to escape/slip away (reflexive). Escapar de = to escape from.

examples.es: Consiguió escapar sin que nadie lo viera.
examples.en: He managed to escape without anyone seeing him.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Cantar bien/mal = to sing well/badly. También: to squeal/confess (colloquial, crime context).

examples.es: Le cantó una canción de cuna al bebé.
examples.en: She sang a lullaby to the baby.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Controlarse = to control oneself/keep calm. Fuera de control = out of control.

examples.es: Es difícil controlar tus emociones en esa situación.
examples.en: It's difficult to control your emotions in that situation.

notes: Regular -ar with c→qu before e. Both physical and figurative attacks.

examples.es: El equipo atacó desde el principio.
examples.en: The team attacked from the start.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Gastar dinero = to spend money. Gastar energía = to use up energy. Gastarse = to wear out/run out.

examples.es: Gastó todos sus ahorros en el viaje.
examples.en: He spent all his savings on the trip.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Ahorrar dinero = to save money. Ahorrar tiempo = to save time. Ahorro (noun) = savings.

examples.es: Intento ahorrar algo de dinero cada mes.
examples.en: I try to save some money every month.

notes: En mi opinión = in my opinion. Dar una opinión = to give an opinion. Cambiar de opinión = to change one's mind.

examples.es: En mi opinión, tiene razón.
examples.en: In my opinion, she is right.

notes: Cause (of an effect) or cause (a campaign/movement). A causa de = because of. Sin causa = without reason.

examples.es: La causa del incendio fue un cortocircuito.
examples.en: The cause of the fire was a short circuit.

notes: Spirit or ghost (el Espíritu Santo = Holy Ghost). Also: the spirit/essence of something. Espíritu de equipo = team spirit.

examples.es: Tiene un espíritu aventurero.
examples.en: She has an adventurous spirit.

notes: Beach or seaside. Ir a la playa = to go to the beach. Playa urbana = urban beach.

examples.es: Pasamos el verano en la playa.
examples.en: We spent the summer at the beach.

notes: Speed or velocity. Límite de velocidad = speed limit. A toda velocidad = at full speed.

examples.es: El coche iba a gran velocidad.
examples.en: The car was going at high speed.

notes: A period of time, era, or season. En aquella época = at that time/in those days. Cada época tiene sus modas.

examples.es: Fue la mejor época de su vida.
examples.en: It was the best period of his life.

notes: A qué distancia = how far away. Mantener la distancia = to keep one's distance. A distancia = remotely/from afar.

examples.es: ¿A qué distancia está el aeropuerto?
examples.en: How far is the airport?

notes: Society (social group) or company (business — Sociedad Anónima = S.A. / plc). Alta sociedad = high society.

examples.es: Vivimos en una sociedad cada vez más conectada.
examples.en: We live in an increasingly connected society.

notes: Market (place to buy/sell) or market (economic). Mercado de valores = stock market. Mercado negro = black market.

examples.es: Compra las verduras en el mercado local.
examples.en: Buy the vegetables at the local market.

notes: Weight (physical) or peso (currency of several Latin American countries). Perder/ganar peso = to lose/gain weight.

examples.es: Quiero perder algo de peso antes del verano.
examples.en: I want to lose some weight before summer.

notes: Effect or result. En efecto = indeed/in fact. Efectos especiales = special effects. Tener efecto = to take effect.

examples.es: El medicamento tuvo un efecto inmediato.
examples.en: The medicine had an immediate effect.

notes: Result or outcome. Como resultado = as a result. Dar resultado = to work/yield results.

examples.es: Los resultados del examen saldrán mañana.
examples.en: The exam results will come out tomorrow.

notes: Any hat with a brim. Sombrero de copa = top hat. Quitarse el sombrero = to take one's hat off (lit. and fig.).

examples.es: Llevaba un sombrero de paja en la playa.
examples.en: She was wearing a straw hat on the beach.

notes: Process (sequence of steps) or legal proceedings (proceso judicial = legal proceedings/trial).

examples.es: Es un proceso largo pero vale la pena.
examples.en: It's a long process but it's worth it.

notes: Chest (body part). Dar el pecho = to breastfeed. A pecho descubierto = bare-chested; also: openly/with nothing to hide.

examples.es: Le dolía el pecho después de correr.
examples.en: His chest hurt after running.

notes: Size or magnitude. ¿De qué tamaño? = What size? Tamaño natural = life-size.

examples.es: ¿Tienes esta camiseta en otro tamaño?
examples.en: Do you have this T-shirt in another size?

examples.es: Fuimos a nadar al lago.
examples.en: We went to swim in the lake.

notes: Community or autonomous region (Comunidad Autónoma = autonomous community, the main administrative division of Spain).

examples.es: Es importante ayudar a la comunidad local.
examples.en: It's important to help the local community.

examples.es: Preparó una sopa de verduras muy rica.
examples.en: She made a very tasty vegetable soup.

notes: Desert (geographical). Also used as adjective: desierto/a = deserted/empty (a desierto street). Predicar en el desierto = to preach to deaf ears.

examples.es: El Sahara es el desierto más grande del mundo.
examples.en: The Sahara is the largest desert in the world.

notes: Nation or country. Naciones Unidas = United Nations. Nacional (adj) = national.

examples.es: Representó a su nación en los Juegos Olímpicos.
examples.en: He represented his nation at the Olympic Games.

notes: A feeling or emotion. Herir los sentimientos de alguien = to hurt someone's feelings.

examples.es: No sé cómo expresar mis sentimientos.
examples.en: I don't know how to express my feelings.

notes: A thought or idea. También: pansy (the flower). El libre pensamiento = free thinking.

examples.es: No puedo quitarme ese pensamiento de la cabeza.
examples.en: I can't get that thought out of my head.

notes: Culture (of a society, arts, or biology). Cultura general = general knowledge. Choque cultural = culture shock.

examples.es: Es un país con una cultura muy rica.
examples.en: It's a country with a very rich culture.

notes: Custom, habit, or tradition. Tener la costumbre de = to be in the habit of. Como de costumbre = as usual.

examples.es: Tiene la costumbre de levantarse muy temprano.
examples.en: She has the habit of getting up very early.

notes: Flower. En flor = in bloom. La flor y la nata = the cream of the crop. Flores silvestres = wildflowers.

examples.es: Le regaló un ramo de flores.
examples.en: He gave her a bunch of flowers.

notes: Emotion or excitement. ¡Qué emoción! = How exciting! Emocional = emotional.

examples.es: La película estuvo llena de emociones.
examples.en: The film was full of emotions.

notes: Will, willpower, or wish. Buena voluntad = goodwill. Fuerza de voluntad = willpower. A voluntad = at will.

examples.es: Tiene una fuerza de voluntad increíble.
examples.en: She has incredible willpower.

notes: Conscience (moral sense) or consciousness/awareness. Tener mala conciencia = to have a guilty conscience. Tomar conciencia de = to become aware of.

examples.es: No puede dormir por la mala conciencia.
examples.en: He can't sleep because of his guilty conscience.

notes: Shoulder (body part). Encogerse de hombros = to shrug. Llevar a hombros = to carry on one's shoulders.

examples.es: Me duelen los hombros de estar sentado.
examples.en: My shoulders hurt from sitting down.

notes: Arrow (weapon or symbol). Also used for arrow signs/indicators (follow the arrows).

examples.es: Sigue las flechas hasta la salida.
examples.en: Follow the arrows to the exit.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Es necesario + inf = it is necessary to. Lo necesario = what is necessary/enough.

examples.es: No es necesario que vengas si no quieres.
examples.en: It's not necessary for you to come if you don't want to.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. En público = in public. Transporte público = public transport. El público = the audience.

examples.es: Este edificio es de uso público.
examples.en: This building is for public use.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Zona peligrosa = danger zone. Peligrosamente = dangerously.

examples.es: Esa zona de la ciudad es muy peligrosa por la noche.
examples.en: That part of the city is very dangerous at night.

notes: Invariable for gender (principal). Agrees in number: principales. El personaje principal = the main character. Calle principal = main street.

examples.es: El problema principal es la falta de comunicación.
examples.en: The main problem is the lack of communication.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Before a noun: former (mi antiguo jefe = my former boss). After a noun: old/ancient (un edificio antiguo = an old building).

examples.es: Vive en un antiguo edificio del siglo XIX.
examples.en: He lives in an old 19th-century building.

notes: Invariable for gender (natural). Agrees in number: naturales. Es natural que = it's natural that. Recursos naturales = natural resources.

examples.es: Prefiero los productos naturales a los artificiales.
examples.en: I prefer natural products to artificial ones.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Sector privado = private sector. Vida privada = private life. En privado = in private.

examples.es: Es una conversación privada.
examples.en: It's a private conversation.

notes: Invariable for gender (nacional). Agrees in number: nacionales. Carretera nacional = A-road/national road.

examples.es: El equipo nacional ganó la copa.
examples.en: The national team won the cup.

notes: Invariable for gender (social). Agrees in number: sociales. Redes sociales = social media/networks.

examples.es: Las redes sociales han cambiado la forma de comunicarnos.
examples.en: Social media has changed the way we communicate.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Also used as a noun: el extranjero = a foreigner; en el extranjero = abroad.

examples.es: Vivió en el extranjero durante cinco años.
examples.en: She lived abroad for five years.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. A paso lento = at a slow pace. Lentamente = slowly. Cocción lenta = slow cooking.

examples.es: El tráfico estaba muy lento esta mañana.
examples.en: The traffic was very slow this morning.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Also: big/serious (un problema gordo = a big problem). El gordo = the big lottery prize (Spain).

examples.es: El problema gordo es que no tenemos dinero.
examples.en: The big problem is that we have no money.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Short in length or duration (not height — for height use bajo). A corto plazo = short-term. Quedarse corto = to underestimate.

examples.es: La película es bastante corta, solo dura una hora.
examples.en: The film is quite short, it only lasts an hour.

notes: Invariable for gender (suave). Agrees in number: suaves. Smooth to the touch, gentle in manner, mild in flavour.

examples.es: La seda es una tela muy suave.
examples.en: Silk is a very smooth fabric.

notes: Invariable for gender (internacional). Agrees in number: internacionales.

examples.es: Es un problema de carácter internacional.
examples.en: It is a problem of an international nature.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Also used as a noun: el político/la política = a politician. La política = politics or policy.

examples.es: Hay que resolver esto por medios políticos.
examples.en: This must be resolved by political means.

notes: Regular -ar verb. In Latin America the standard word for driving a car (Spain uses conducir). Also: to handle/manage (una situación difícil).

examples.es: ¿Sabes manejar un camión?
examples.en: Do you know how to drive a truck?

notes: Regular -ar verb. Disparar un arma = to fire a weapon. Disparar una foto = to take a shot (photography). Dispararse = to skyrocket (prices).

examples.es: Se oyó un disparo en la noche.
examples.en: A shot was heard in the night.

notes: Regular -ar with z→c before e. To throw, launch, or release. Lanzar un producto = to launch a product. Lanzarse = to dive in/take the plunge.

examples.es: El atleta lanzó el disco muy lejos.
examples.en: The athlete threw the discus very far.

notes: Irregular yo: convenzo (c→z before a/o). Convencer a alguien de algo = to convince someone of something. Convencerse = to convince oneself.

examples.es: Intentó convencerme de que tenía razón.
examples.en: She tried to convince me that she was right.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Votar por = to vote for. Votar en contra = to vote against. Derecho a voto = right to vote.

examples.es: Es importante votar en las elecciones.
examples.en: It's important to vote in elections.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Dudar de = to doubt/be suspicious of. Dudar si = to wonder whether. Sin dudar = without hesitation.

examples.es: No dudes en llamarme si necesitas algo.
examples.en: Don't hesitate to call me if you need anything.

notes: Regular -ar verb. Planear un viaje/una boda = to plan a trip/a wedding. Also: to glide (birds, planes).

examples.es: Planeamos ir de vacaciones en agosto.
examples.en: We're planning to go on holiday in August.

notes: Regular -ar with z→c before e. Organizar un evento = to organise an event. Organizarse = to get organised.

examples.es: ¿Quién organizó esta reunión?
examples.en: Who organised this meeting?

notes: A crime (usually serious — murder, etc.). Cf. delito (any criminal offence, including minor ones). Crimen organizado = organised crime.

examples.es: La policía investigó el crimen.
examples.en: The police investigated the crime.

notes: Honour or integrity. En honor a la verdad = to tell the truth. Palabra de honor = word of honour. Honores militares = military honours.

examples.es: Lo hizo por honor, no por dinero.
examples.en: He did it for honour, not for money.

notes: A doubt or question. Sin duda = without doubt/certainly. Tener dudas = to have doubts. Poner en duda = to call into question.

examples.es: Si tienes alguna duda, pregúntame.
examples.en: If you have any questions, ask me.

notes: Hope or expectation. Perder la esperanza = to lose hope. Con la esperanza de = in the hope of.

examples.es: Nunca pierdas la esperanza.
examples.en: Never lose hope.

notes: Multiple meanings: note (written), grade/mark (academic), musical note. Sacar buena nota = to get a good grade. Tomar nota = to take note.

examples.es: Sacó muy buenas notas en los exámenes.
examples.en: She got very good grades in the exams.

notes: Feminine noun, always singular in most uses. Fe en = faith in. De buena/mala fe = in good/bad faith. Acta de fe = act of faith.

examples.es: Tiene una fe ciega en sus hijos.
examples.en: She has blind faith in her children.

notes: Gender-common: el/la colega. Colleague or (informally) mate/pal. Very common in informal speech throughout Spain and Latin America.

examples.es: Salí a cenar con unos colegas del trabajo.
examples.en: I went out to dinner with some work colleagues.

notes: Shame or embarrassment. Tener vergüenza = to feel ashamed/embarrassed. ¡Qué vergüenza! = How embarrassing! / Shame on you! Sin vergüenza = shameless.

examples.es: Me da vergüenza hablar en público.
examples.en: I feel embarrassed speaking in public.

notes: A wound or injury. Herida abierta = open wound. Also figurative: herida emocional = emotional wound. Herir = to wound.

examples.es: La herida tardó semanas en cicatrizar.
examples.en: The wound took weeks to heal.

notes: A road or highway (between towns). Cf. calle (urban street) and autopista (motorway). Carretera nacional = A-road.

examples.es: Hay mucho tráfico en la carretera esta mañana.
examples.en: There's a lot of traffic on the road this morning.

notes: Note plural: exámenes (accent drops). Hacer/presentar un examen = to sit an exam. Suspender/aprobar un examen = to fail/pass an exam.

examples.es: Tengo un examen muy importante mañana.
examples.en: I have a very important exam tomorrow.

examples.es: El vuelo sale del aeropuerto a las ocho.
examples.en: The flight leaves from the airport at eight.

notes: Revenge or vengeance. Tomar venganza = to take revenge. Por venganza = out of revenge.

examples.es: Actuó movido por la venganza.
examples.en: He was driven by revenge.

notes: A shirt (with collar and buttons). Camisa de fuerza = straitjacket. En mangas de camisa = in shirtsleeves.

examples.es: Lleva una camisa azul y una corbata.
examples.en: He's wearing a blue shirt and a tie.

notes: The stomach (organ or the belly area). Dolor de estómago = stomachache. Tener buen estómago = to have a strong stomach.

examples.es: Me duele el estómago después de comer.
examples.en: My stomach hurts after eating.

notes: Joy, happiness, or delight. ¡Qué alegría! = How wonderful! / What great news! Dar alegría = to bring joy.

examples.es: La noticia les llenó de alegría.
examples.en: The news filled them with joy.

notes: A miracle. ¡Es un milagro! = It's a miracle! De milagro = miraculously/by a miracle.

examples.es: Sobrevivió de milagro al accidente.
examples.en: He survived the accident by a miracle.

notes: A private office or study. Distinct from oficina (open-plan office). Also: dispatch/sending of goods.

examples.es: El director está en su despacho.
examples.en: The director is in his office.

notes: A rule, regulation, or ruler (measuring tool). En regla = in order/according to the rules. Por regla general = as a general rule.

examples.es: Las reglas del juego son muy sencillas.
examples.en: The rules of the game are very simple.

examples.es: Llamaron a una ambulancia de inmediato.
examples.en: They called an ambulance immediately.

notes: Pride (the feeling). Sentir orgullo de = to feel proud of. A distinction from el orgulloso (the proud person).

examples.es: Siente un gran orgullo por sus logros.
examples.en: He feels great pride in his achievements.

notes: Port or harbour. Also: mountain pass (puerto de montaña). Puerto USB/HDMI = USB/HDMI port (technology).

examples.es: El barco llegó al puerto al amanecer.
examples.en: The ship arrived at the port at dawn.

notes: Title (of a book, person, or rank), academic degree, or certificate. Título universitario = university degree.

examples.es: Obtuvo el título de ingeniero el año pasado.
examples.en: He obtained his engineering degree last year.

notes: Fever or high temperature. Tener fiebre = to have a fever. Fiebre del oro = gold rush.

examples.es: El niño tiene mucha fiebre, hay que llamar al médico.
examples.en: The child has a high fever, we need to call the doctor.

notes: A criminal offence or crime (any severity). Cf. crimen (serious crime). Delito leve = minor offence. Cometer un delito = to commit an offence.

examples.es: Conducir borracho es un delito grave.
examples.en: Drink-driving is a serious offence.

notes: Egg. Huevo frito/revuelto/duro = fried/scrambled/hard-boiled egg. Note: in some Latin American countries huevos is a vulgar term, so care is advised.

examples.es: ¿Cómo quieres los huevos, fritos o revueltos?
examples.en: How do you want your eggs, fried or scrambled?

notes: Short for motocicleta. Ir en moto = to ride a motorbike. Moto de agua = jet ski.

examples.es: Va al trabajo en moto todos los días.
examples.en: He goes to work by motorbike every day.

notes: Salary or wage. Subida de sueldo = pay rise. Sueldo mínimo = minimum wage.

examples.es: Acaba de conseguir una subida de sueldo.
examples.en: She just got a pay rise.

notes: Multiple meanings: leaf (of a plant), sheet (of paper), blade (of a knife). Hoja de cálculo = spreadsheet. En blanco = blank sheet.

examples.es: Las hojas del árbol cambian de color en otoño.
examples.en: The tree's leaves change colour in autumn.

notes: Betrayal or treason. Alta traición = high treason. A traición = treacherously/from behind.

examples.es: Lo que hizo fue una traición imperdonable.
examples.en: What he did was an unforgivable betrayal.

notes: Orange (the fruit). As an adjective (colour): invariable — una camiseta naranja. Zumo/jugo de naranja = orange juice.

examples.es: Tomé un zumo de naranja en el desayuno.
examples.en: I had an orange juice at breakfast.

notes: Loyalty or fidelity. Con lealtad = loyally. Lealtad a la marca = brand loyalty.

examples.es: La lealtad es una de las virtudes más importantes.
examples.en: Loyalty is one of the most important virtues.

notes: A jacket (lighter than an abrigo/coat). Chaqueta de punto = cardigan.

examples.es: Coge una chaqueta, que hace frío fuera.
examples.en: Grab a jacket, it's cold outside.

notes: Overcoat or coat. Al abrigo de = sheltered from / under the protection of.

examples.es: Necesitas un buen abrigo para el invierno.
examples.en: You need a good coat for winter.

notes: Recipe (cooking) or prescription (medical). Seguir una receta = to follow a recipe. Receta médica = doctor's prescription.

examples.es: ¿Me das la receta de ese pastel?
examples.en: Can you give me the recipe for that cake?

examples.es: Respeto todas las religiones del mundo.
examples.en: I respect all religions in the world.

notes: Agrees in gender (invariable: grave for masc and fem). Agrees in number: graves. Estar grave = to be seriously ill. Un error grave = a serious mistake.

examples.es: El paciente está en estado grave.
examples.en: The patient is in a critical condition.

notes: Invariable for gender (inútil). Agrees in number: inútiles. Also used as a noun: un inútil = a useless person.

examples.es: Este aparato es completamente inútil.
examples.en: This device is completely useless.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Literal: deep (water, hole). Figurative: profound (thought, feeling). Respiración profunda = deep breathing.

examples.es: El lago es muy profundo en este punto.
examples.en: The lake is very deep at this point.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Ser famoso/a = to be famous. Hacerse famoso = to become famous.

examples.es: Es un cantante muy famoso en todo el mundo.
examples.en: He's a very famous singer all over the world.

notes: Invariable for gender (útil). Agrees in number: útiles. Días útiles = working days. Lo útil = the useful thing.

examples.es: Este diccionario me resulta muy útil.
examples.en: I find this dictionary very useful.

notes: Invariable for gender (urgente). Agrees in number: urgentes. Correo urgente = express mail. Con carácter urgente = as a matter of urgency.

examples.es: Necesito hablar contigo, es urgente.
examples.en: I need to talk to you, it's urgent.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Also used as a noun: un desconocido/una desconocida = a stranger. Lo desconocido = the unknown.

examples.es: Me llamó un número desconocido.
examples.en: An unknown number called me.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. ¡Es muy típico de él! = That's so typical of him! Comida típica = traditional/typical food.

examples.es: Es un plato típico de la región.
examples.en: It's a typical dish from the region.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. Also used as a noun: el científico/la científica = the scientist.

examples.es: Los avances científicos cambian nuestra vida.
examples.en: Scientific advances change our lives.

notes: Agrees in gender/number. More respectful than viejo. Also used as a noun: el anciano/la anciana = an elderly person/man/woman.

examples.es: Ayudó a la anciana a cruzar la calle.
examples.en: He helped the elderly woman cross the street.

notes: Very common copulative verb. 'Me parece' = it seems to me. Yo parezco (irregular yo).

examples.es: Parece que va a llover.
examples.en: It seems like it's going to rain.

examples.es: Me parece una buena idea.
examples.en: It seems like a good idea to me.

notes: Often used reflexively: cuidarse = to take care of oneself. Cuidar de = to look after.

examples.es: Cuida a los niños mientras salgo.
examples.en: Take care of the children while I go out.

examples.es: Debes cuidarte más.
examples.en: You should take better care of yourself.

notes: Common in polite requests: 'no quisiera molestarte' = I wouldn't want to bother you. Also: to annoy, to disturb.

examples.es: ¿Te molesta el ruido?
examples.en: Does the noise bother you?

examples.es: No quiero molestar.
examples.en: I don't want to be a bother.

notes: Usually reflexive: preocuparse (por) = to worry (about). 'No te preocupes' = Don't worry.

examples.es: No te preocupes por eso.
examples.en: Don't worry about that.

examples.es: Me preocupa su salud.
examples.en: His health worries me.

notes: Also means to introduce people: 'te presento a mi amigo' = let me introduce you to my friend.

examples.es: Te presento a mi hermana.
examples.en: Let me introduce you to my sister.

examples.es: Presentó su informe al jefe.
examples.en: He submitted his report to the boss.

notes: Also used reflexively: sorprenderse = to be surprised. Noun: sorpresa.

examples.es: Me sorprendió su reacción.
examples.en: His reaction surprised me.

examples.es: No me sorprende.
examples.en: It doesn't surprise me.

notes: Stem-changing e→ie. Often reflexive: despertarse = to wake up (oneself). Also: to awaken (interest etc.).

examples.es: Me desperté tarde esta mañana.
examples.en: I woke up late this morning.

examples.es: El ruido despertó a los niños.
examples.en: The noise woke up the children.

notes: Irregular past participle: descubierto. Otherwise regular -ir. Noun: descubrimiento.

examples.es: Descubrió la verdad demasiado tarde.
examples.en: He discovered the truth too late.

examples.es: Han descubierto una nueva especie.
examples.en: They have discovered a new species.

notes: Stem-changing o→ue. Irregular past participle: resuelto. Noun: resolución.

examples.es: Tenemos que resolver este problema.
examples.en: We have to solve this problem.

examples.es: El conflicto se resolvió rápidamente.
examples.en: The conflict was resolved quickly.

notes: Covers physical fights and arguments. Pelearse (con) = to argue/fight with. Noun: pelea.

examples.es: Los hermanos siempre están peleando.
examples.en: The brothers are always fighting.

examples.es: No quiero pelear contigo.
examples.en: I don't want to fight with you.

notes: Stem-changing e→ie. Noun: defensa, defensor.

examples.es: Defendió su tesis brillantemente.
examples.en: He defended his thesis brilliantly.

examples.es: Siempre te defenderé.
examples.en: I will always defend you.

notes: Also means to hold/conduct an event: 'se celebró una reunión' = a meeting was held.

examples.es: Vamos a celebrar tu cumpleaños.
examples.en: We're going to celebrate your birthday.

examples.es: La boda se celebró en la iglesia.
examples.en: The wedding was held in the church.

notes: Also means to treat/pay for someone: 'te invito' = it's on me / I'll treat you.

examples.es: Te invito a cenar.
examples.en: I'll treat you to dinner.

examples.es: Me invitó a su fiesta.
examples.en: She invited me to her party.

notes: Disfrutar de = to enjoy (something). Very common in everyday speech.
